pages.text: The snow stopped that morning. Big jars stood side by side in the yard, with soft snow on each lid. Little birds perched on the branch above.
"What do bird footprints look like in snow?" Yuki stood close to the door. "I really want to see."
A bird landed softly beside a jar. Yuki flung open the door and ran outside.
The birds fluttered away. Only Yuki's footprints remained beside the jars.
Yuki ran this way and that. "Here? Over there?"
Yuki's footprints crushed the place where the bird had landed.
Crouching and looking closely, Yuki saw no bird prints at all. "They're all gone."
Grandma asked, "Who went out first, before the birds came?" Yuki looked down at their own feet.
The next morning, Yuki sat on the porch and waited, gently holding Momo around the neck and keeping still.
A bird walked over the snow beside a jar, leaving marks of three toes each time. Yuki quietly watched from the porch.
